chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Hasani who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about completing (the prayer) and shortening (it). He said: 'When you enter the two Sanctuaries, intend ten days and complete the prayer.' I said to him: 'I arrive in Mecca one or two or three days before Tawree (the 8th of Dhu al-Qi'dah).' He said: 'Intend a stay of ten days and complete the prayer.'

key_terms.التَّوْرِيَةِ: The day of departure for Mina (8th of Dhu al-Qi'dah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening or completing prayers for travelers entering Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahaniyyah clarifies the juristic principle that the status of a traveler (musafir) is determined by the intention of stay rather than the actual duration, specifically within the sanctified boundaries of Mecca and Medina. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that intending a ten-day stay upon entering the Haram qualifies one as a resident (muqim) for prayer purposes, even if arrival precedes the standard days of Hajj. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh, allowing travelers to maintain the convenience of shortening prayers until they formally commit to a ten-day residence.
